**Layer 1 shipped as `b619444cc`.** Layers 2 and 3 are accounted for below.

## What landed

`scripts/check-extension-core-diff.ts` + self-test, registered in `script-test-manifest.ts` so `test:scripts` runs it. 5 rows, all green.

Base resolution, in order: `ULTRAWORKERS_SEAM_BASE` → `ULTRAWORKERS_TEST_DIFF_BASE` (the repo's existing spelling, which CI already sets on every TS test job) → `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`. **A tree it cannot measure exits NON-ZERO.** That is the file's reason for existing: `epic-jwsy.14` abstained, exited 0, and a CI badge read it as a pass.

Proven able to fail, as the bead demands. Mutating `CORE_PREFIX` to a value that cannot match turns three rows red — including the falsifier row that commits a `packages/` change and requires exit 1. Restored byte-identically (`shasum 6313e22728a4da7f60377b520b7d1882cbad732b`) and re-verified. The falsifier builds **real temp repositories**, because the property is what `git diff <base>...HEAD` reports for a tree; a stub would only prove the right function was called.

## Layers 2 and 3 — already accounted for, by someone else

- **Layer 3 landed in `f65a4ac4f5`** as `packages/coding-agent/test/outsider-seam-guard.test.ts`, and it is good work: it states in its own docblock what it does NOT prove (no `workflow` coverage, no panel mount) and why. Verified green.
- **Layer 2** (the five seams reached by *this epic's* extension) is correctly deferred — `extensions/workflow.ts` does not exist. It should land with bead `.12`, not before.

So `.1` is not blocked on me; it is blocked on the entrypoint existing.

## The finding: the guard for "no core diff" is itself stored in core

Measured from the epic's first commit `31ef54e8f2`:

```
$ ULTRAWORKERS_SEAM_BASE=31ef54e8f2 bun scripts/check-extension-core-diff.ts
FAIL — 2 core path(s) changed
  packages/coding-agent/test/outsider-seam-guard.test.ts
  packages/peer/test/transport.test.ts
```

Layer 3's test living under `packages/` means the layer-1 gate can never report clean while layer 3 exists there. That is a genuine structural tension, not a defect in either file. Options, none of which I took unilaterally:

1. Layer 1 measures against a base that excludes the guard's own landing (feels like special-casing, and special cases rot);
2. The seam tests move outside `packages/` — consistent with the epic's own criterion and with the plan's `test/extensions/` path, but that is another session's committed file;
3. Layer 1 scopes to the epic's *deliverable* tree rather than all of `packages/`.

**This needs an owner ruling.** I did not move another session's committed test.

## Not wired into `check:ts`, with the measurement that says why

- from `merge-base origin/main HEAD`: **2263** core paths. This branch carries the whole programme, so adding the gate to `check-chain` MEMBERS would turn `check:ts` red for reasons unrelated to the criterion — a gate that cries wolf on day one is a gate that gets deleted.
- from the epic base: **2** (above).

The `package.json` script key **is** wired (`check:extension-core-diff`), so the gate is runnable on demand with an explicit base. Adding it to `MEMBERS` should happen once the base semantics above are settled — that is the same decision as the finding.

## Smaller notes

- `crates/` is deliberately out of scope: the bead's criterion is `packages/`, and widening it is a programme decision. One line plus a test row if it is made.
- Base prefix matching accepts `\` as well as `/`, because a caller assembling the changed-file list on Windows would otherwise get a real core change read as clean — and it would be green in CI, which is where the miss is read as a verdict.

title: [GUARD] The cut ledger — 11 measured cuts and 8 deliberate absences, made executable
description:
THE CUT LEDGER, made executable. Exists so that a future agent "helpfully" restores something we
deliberately dropped.

## Why

The reference repo is 24,740 LOC. We are taking ~6,700. Every one of those cut lines is a
decision someone will eventually question — and "it was in the reference, so I put it back" is the
default move. This bead makes each cut a recorded, checkable decision instead.

**A cut that is not written down is a cut that gets undone by accident.**

## Do NOT restore — measured reasons

| Cut file | ref LOC | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `workflow-comprehension.ts` | 1673 | Generates markdown from capability descriptors. We have our own skill system; this would produce docs describing a surface that is not shipped. |
| `workflow-authoring-coverage.ts` | 502 | Checks that the docs match the code. Self-referential once we author our own docs; it validates a generator we deliberately cut. |
| `deep-research.ts` | 135 | **Does not verify.** Measured at `:61-67`: the Verify phase is ONE `agent()` call, one pass, no voting. `minSupport` (default 2, `:34`) is INTERPOLATED INTO THE PROMPT, not enforced in code, and the clause "OR by one clearly authoritative source" lets a claim pass on ONE source. `verdict.discarded` is requested by the schema (`:66`) and never read (`:77`). |
| `usage-limit-scheduler.ts` | 566 | No usage-limit pausing here. Adapting it means inventing a quota concept we do not have. |
| `agent-registry.ts` | 233 | pi agent types (`AgentDefinition`, `resolveAgentType`). We have no equivalent; this is host-specific surface area. |
| `workflow-release-gate.ts` | 526 | Their release gate. Ours is `scripts/check:ts` + `bun run test:scripts`. Two release gates is worse than one. |
| `code-review.ts` | 183 | A workflow instance, not engine surface. Belongs in user scripts. |
| `workflow-context-measurement.ts` | 262 | Measures context growth for THEIR UI; ours will be measured against our own renderer. |
| `adoptLiveRunsToSession` | ~40 in manager | Their session-id ownership model. Ours has no equivalent concept to adopt into. |
| capability `capabilities` descriptors | ~330 in contract | Generates markdown. Cut with the generators. |
| `AGENT_OPTIONS` option shapes | ~90 in contract | Same — documentation shapes, not runtime. |

## Do NOT build — measured absences in the reference

These are NOT oversights. Each was measured, found absent, and decided against.

| Not building | Evidence |
|---|---|
| An `f` key | Filter is `/`. Grepping `"f"` in `workflow-ui.ts` returns nothing. `ctrl+f` is page-down. |
| Elapsed time in the navigator | Grep `duration\|elapsed\|startedAt\|Date.now` in `workflow-ui.ts` returns NOTHING. It exists only in `/workflows status` (`workflow-commands.ts:114`) and the completion line. |
| Panel input handling | `task-panel.ts:1761-1762`: "Purely informational... the panel takes no input." No `Focusable`, no `handleInput`. Expansion is `/workflows`, full stop. |
| A "replayed agent" badge | `WorkflowAgentSnapshot` (`display.ts:10-35`) has no `replayed` field. |
| `unverified` vs `refuted` | Exists nowhere in the reference. Not a field, not a bucket, not a prompt word — only the phrase "claims unverified" inside one prompt string at `:1593`. |
| `rm` at tool level | Slash command only (`workflow-commands.ts:286-289`). Deletion is destructive; it stays a human action. |
| Conditional persistence | `WorkflowSettings` (`:13-74`) has no consent field. |
| A new worker selector | Workflows run in-process. All 16 existing selectors derive from `WORKER_HOST_SELECTOR_PREFIX` (`utils/src/worker-host.ts:18`). Adding one would violate the worker rule that issue #1150 exists to enforce. |

## The one place we deliberately do BETTER

Recorded so it is not "simplified" back to parity: `workflow-manager.ts:212` already tracks
`replayedAgentCalls` internally but never puts it on the snapshot, so a resumed run is
indistinguishable from a fresh one. Adding that badge is an improvement, not a missing feature.

## What to assert

For each row marked CUT: a check that the named file/symbol is absent from our tree. This is a
negative-contract test — legitimate per AGENTS.md because each row prevents a documented leak back
in.

For each row marked "do NOT build": an assertion of required ABSENCE in the shipped UI. Also a
negative contract.
## Definition of done

This guard is DONE when, for every row in the ledger above:

    there is an executable assertion that the cut file/symbol is ABSENT
        from our tree
    AND there is an executable assertion that the deliberately-absent
        behaviour is ABSENT from the shipped UI

and, again, a deliberately violated ledger — restore ONE cut file, or add
an `f` keybinding — makes the guard go RED.

A ledger written as prose is a document. A ledger written as assertions is a
guard. Only the second one prevents an accidental restore.

## The deliberate-improvement carve-out

The one row marked "opportunity to do better" (the replay badge) must NOT
be asserted absent. It is the single intended divergence from parity, and a
guard that forbids it would block the improvement.

## Dependencies

None.

title: P1 — Engine: parseWorkflowScript + vm sandbox + determinism prelude
description:
Copy `parseWorkflowScript` and the vm sandbox from `.tmp/ref/pi-dynamic-workflows`.

Copy source: `src/workflow.ts:2011-2071` (parse), `:1799-1817` (sandbox),
`:529-546` (prelude), `:514` (blocklist).

## Why this is first

Nothing downstream can be trusted until a script that says `export const meta` is the only shape
that runs, and until a script that calls `Math.random` cannot. Every later phase assumes both.

## 1.1 parseWorkflowScript — `workflow.ts:2011-2071`

**Check order must not be reversed.** Blocklist first, AST second. The blocklist catches
`Date.now()` spelled with spaces (`Date . now`); the AST catches `export const meta` in the wrong
position. Reversing them loses a layer.

| # | Check | ref line | Error when violated |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Blocklist | `:2012-2018` | `SCRIPT_VALIDATION_ERROR`, `recoverable: false` |
| 2 | `parse(...)` | `:2020-2026` | — |
| 3 | `ast.body[0].type === "ExportNamedDeclaration"` | `:2028-2035` | `export const meta = ... must be the first statement in the script` |
| 4 | `declaration.kind === "const"` | `:2038-2046` | `meta export must be 'export const meta = ...'` |
| 5 | exactly one declarator | `:2047-2051` | `meta export must declare only 'meta'` |
| 6 | identifier named exactly `meta` | `:2053-2058` | — |
| 7 | has an initializer | `:2059-2062` | `meta must have a literal value` |
| 8 | `evaluateLiteral` + `validateMeta` | `:2064-2065` | — |
| 9 | strip the export from the body | `:2069` | `script.slice(0, first.start) + script.slice(first.end)` |

Blocklist verbatim (`:514`):

    const DETERMINISM_BLOCKLIST = /\bDate\s*\.\s*now\b|\bMath\s*\.\s*random\b|\bnew\s+Date\s*\(\s*\)/;

### SWAP THE PARSER — the one required deviation

The reference imports `acorn` (`workflow.ts:3-4`). **We do not have acorn.** We have
`@babel/parser` ^7.29.7 — `package.json:17`, a catalog dependency, already installed.

    // reference
    import { parse } from "acorn";
    parse(script, { ecmaVersion: "latest", sourceType: "module",
                   allowAwaitOutsideFunction: true, allowReturnOutsideFunction: true, ranges: false })

    // ours
    import { parse } from "@babel/parser";
    parse(code, { sourceType: "module", plugins: ["topLevelAwait"] })

Keep the eight-step logic byte-for-byte in behaviour. Change only the AST layer. The node type
names differ (`ExportNamedDeclaration` and `VariableDeclaration` exist in both; check the rest
against babel's AST rather than assuming acorn's).

Do NOT add acorn to the workspace. The dependency exists and is catalogued.

### evaluateLiteral — `:2073-2109`

Accepts ONLY: `ObjectExpression`, `ArrayExpression`, `Literal`, non-interpolated
`TemplateLiteral`, negative-number `UnaryExpression`.

Rejects: spread, computed keys, methods, accessors, sparse arrays, interpolated templates.

**Keep the prototype-pollution guard verbatim** (`:2083-2085`):

    if (key === "__proto__" || key === "constructor" || key === "prototype") {
      throw new Error(`reserved key name not allowed in ${path}: ${key}`);
    }

### validateMeta — `:2118-2133`

- `name`, `description`: required non-empty strings
- `model`: must be a string if present
- `phases`: array, each element has a string `title`

**Unknown keys are NOT rejected.** Meta is permissive on extras. Keep that — a workflow author
adding a comment field is not an error.

## 1.2 The sandbox — `:1799-1817`

    const { globals: projectGlobals, diagnostics } =
      WORKFLOW_CAPABILITY_CONTRACT.assembleRuntimeBindings(runtimeImplementations);
    const context = vm.createContext({
      ...projectGlobals,
      // Object/Array/JSON/Math/Date/Promise/Set/Map... come from the vm realm itself.
      // We deliberately do NOT inject host built-ins: their .constructor would be the
      // host Function (a determinism-guard bypass).
    });
    const wrapped = `${DETERMINISM_PRELUDE}\n(async () => {\n${body}\n})()`;
    const result = await new vm.Script(wrapped, { filename: `${meta.name || "workflow"}.js` })
      .runInContext(context);

**Scripts have no `import`.** The body is wrapped in an IIFE. There is no module resolution.

`assembleRuntimeBindings` comes from the capability-contract phase — until that lands, stub it to
return an empty globals object so this phase can land first.

## 1.3 DETERMINISM_PRELUDE — `:529-546` VERBATIM

This is a CONTRACT, not a hardening option. Remove it and the restart key and resume become lies:
a re-run would produce different values than the cached journal.

    const DETERMINISM_PRELUDE = [
      '"use strict";',
      'Math.random = () => { throw new Error("Math.random() is unavailable in a workflow (it breaks resume); pass randomness via args or vary by index"); };',
      "{",
      "  const RealDate = Date;",
      '  const fail = (w) => { throw new Error(w + " is unavailable in a workflow (it breaks resume); pass a timestamp via args"); };',
      "  const SafeDate = function (...a) {",
      '    if (!new.target) fail("Date()");',
      '    if (a.length === 0) fail("new Date()");',
      "    return Reflect.construct(RealDate, a, SafeDate);",
      "  };",
      "  SafeDate.UTC = RealDate.UTC;",
      "  SafeDate.parse = RealDate.parse;",
      '  SafeDate.now = () => fail("Date.now()");',
      "  SafeDate.prototype = RealDate.prototype;",
      "  globalThis.Date = SafeDate;",
      "}",
    ].join("\n");

`SafeDate.UTC`, `SafeDate.parse`, and `SafeDate.prototype` MUST survive — a script parses dates
the user passed in. Only the no-arg forms throw.

## Tests (each names a consumer-observable failure)

    test/workflow/parse.test.ts
      - meta not first statement          → SCRIPT_VALIDATION_ERROR
      - `export let meta` / `export var`   → rejected at step 4
      - two declarators in one export     → rejected at step 5
      - `export let meta; meta = {...}`    → rejected at step 7 (no initializer)
      - `__proto__` key in meta literal    → rejected at step 8 (prototype pollution)
      - unknown extra key in meta          → ACCEPTED (permissive, per :2118-2133)

    test/workflow/determinism.test.ts
      - Math.random()      throws
      - Date.now()         throws
      - Date()             throws
      - new Date()         throws

      - new Date("2026-01-01")           STILL WORKS   <- the negative case

title: P2 — Capability contract: injectable globals, the three-level customisation surface
description:
THE API EXPORT LAYER. This bead is the answer to "export APIs so users can fully customise" —
and it is a copy, not a new design.

Copy source: `src/workflow-capability-contract.ts`, of which we take ~180 of 848 LOC.

## Why this lands BEFORE the agent bridge

`WorkflowRuntimeImplementations` declares `agent: unknown`. That declaration IS the seam we plug
the bridge into. Build the bridge first and the contract has to be retrofitted around a concrete
implementation — which is exactly the hardcoding we are removing. Build the contract first and the
bridge becomes a one-line injection.

## 2.1 The interface — `workflow-capability-contract.ts:113-132`

    export interface WorkflowRuntimeImplementations {
      agent: unknown; parallel: unknown; pipeline: unknown; workflow: unknown;
      verify: unknown; judgePanel: unknown; loopUntilDry: unknown; completenessCheck: unknown;
      retry: unknown; gate: unknown; checkpoint: unknown; log: unknown; phase: unknown;
      args: unknown; cwd: unknown; process: unknown; budget: unknown; console: unknown;
    }

**`unknown`, not concrete types.** This is the entire point. The contract does not constrain the
implementation. An owner may pass `agent` as their own function, a wrapper around
`runStructuredSubagent`, an IRC dispatch, a worktree-isolated spawn — the contract does not care
and does not need to change.

If you find yourself wanting to type `agent: (prompt: string, opts: AgentOptions) => Promise<unknown>`
instead, STOP. That single change removes the entire customisation surface and nothing else in
this bead explains why.

## 2.2 The three levels of customisation — this is what we are shipping

**Level 1 — the script DSL.** Nineteen globals injected into the vm realm:

    agent, parallel, pipeline, workflow, verify, judgePanel, loopUntilDry,
    completenessCheck, retry, gate, checkpoint, log, phase,
    args, cwd, process, budget, console

**Level 2 — the runtime, with owner-supplied deps.** `assembleRuntimeBindings(impls)` returns
`{ globals, diagnostics }` (`:107-110`). A caller does:

    const { globals, diagnostics } =
      WORKFLOW_CAPABILITY_CONTRACT.assembleRuntimeBindings({
        agent: myAgent,          // anything
        parallel: myParallel,    // anything
        // ... 17 more
      });
    const context = vm.createContext({ ...globals });

The engine does not change by a single line. THIS is the "full custom" answer.

**Level 3 — replace the engine entirely.** `Workflow` is a tool registered by an extension. Not
wanting it means not registering it means it does not exist. A full replacement is an extension
registering a tool of the same name.

## 2.3 assembleRuntimeBindings + diagnoseAlignment

- `RuntimeBindingAssembly` — `:107-110`: `{ globals, diagnostics }`
- `diagnoseAlignment(evidence)` — `:154-159` signature, `:787-837` implementation. Takes
  `{ suppliedImplementations?, observedProjectGlobals? }`, returns `CapabilityDiagnostic[]`.
- `deepFreeze` — `:839-845`, called once inside `defineWorkflowCapabilityContract` (`:681`).

**diagnoseAlignment is a TEST tool.** Its job: compare what the script declared against what the
engine actually injected, and name the difference. A script declaring 19 globals where the engine
injects 18 must fail with the missing global's NAME — not with a count, which is a weaker claim.

## 2.4 What we CUT from this file — do not restore

| Cut | ref size | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `capabilities` descriptor array | ~330 LOC (`:316-644`) | It generates markdown. We have our own skill system; the cut-ledger bead covers this. |
| `AGENT_OPTIONS`, `CHECKPOINT_OPTIONS`, `VERIFY_OPTIONS`, `JUDGE_PANEL_OPTIONS`, `LOOP_UNTIL_DRY_OPTIONS`, `RETRY_OPTIONS`, `GATE_OPTIONS`, `PHASE_OPTIONS` | ~90 LOC (`:174-260`) | Documentation shapes. Same reason. |
| `projectStaticReferenceFacts` | — | Same. |

`capabilities` being cut means `WORKFLOW_CAPABILITY_DEFINITION` (`:647-678`) and
`defineWorkflowCapabilityContract` (`:681-785`) shrink to just the validation and assembly paths.
That is expected — do not pad them back out to match the reference's shape.

## Tests

    test/workflow/contract.test.ts
      - all 19 globals injected; script declaring 19 succeeds
      - injecting 18 ⇒ diagnoseAlignment names the MISSING ONE (not "1 missing")
      - a caller supplies all-custom `agent` ⇒ engine runs unchanged  <- the customisation proof
      - a caller supplies a throwing `parallel` ⇒ that error surfaces, not a wrapped one
      - deepFreeze: mutating the contract object throws or is a no-op in strict mode

The third row is the one that matters. If it fails, customisation is decorative.

title: P3 — Agent bridge: agent() returns null, adapter to runStructuredSubagent, recursion block
description:
Wire `agent()` to the host's subagent runtime. This is where `node:vm` meets `runStructuredSubagent`.

## 3.1 agent() returns null, NEVER throws

This is the contract. Copy the shape at `workflow.ts:758-760`:

    export type AgentRunResult<TSchemaDef extends TSchema | undefined> =
      TSchemaDef extends TSchema ? /* validated object */ : string;

And the emptiness check at `:2346-2348`:

    function isEmptyTextAgentResult(result: unknown, schema: TSchema | undefined): boolean {
      return schema === undefined && typeof result === "string" && result.trim().length === 0;
    }

**An agent WITH a schema bypasses the emptiness check.** Valid structured data may legitimately
be empty. A prelude-style check that rejects all-empty results would discard real data.

The same shape appears in the plan's own history as bug #87501: a message reporting
`success: true` for a message that was never received. Returning `null` on failure — a value the
script must handle — rather than throwing, means a failed agent is DATA the script branches on.

## 3.2 The adapter

`WorkflowAgentRunner` (`workflow.ts:182-184`) is the seam:

    export interface WorkflowAgentRunner {
      run(prompt: string, options?: AgentRunOptions<TSchema>): Promise<unknown>;
    }

Implement it over `runStructuredSubagent` (`packages/coding-agent/src/task/structured-subagent.ts:707`):

    {
      session, invocationKind: "task",
      assignment: prompt,
      outputSchema: options.schema,     // presence, not truthiness = highest priority (:110)
      model: options.model, effort: options.effort, signal: options.signal,
      onProgress: options.onProgress,
      blockedAgent: <parent agent name>, // blocks recursion, see 3.4
      maxRuntimeMs: options.timeoutMs ?? 0,
    }

### Reading the result — the trap

`result.result.structuredOutput` is `StructuredSubagentOutput`
(`packages/tui/src/tools/task.ts:2119-2126`):

    { source, mode, status: "valid" | "invalid" | "unavailable", data?, error? }

**`data` is PRESENT even when strict validation REJECTS it.** Check `status === "valid"` before
trusting `data`. Reading `data` directly reports a schema violation as a success — the same
success/failure inversion as #87501, one layer down.

This is why a strict-mode violation keeps the parsed-but-invalid payload: it is for diagnostics.
Diagnostics are not results.

## 3.3 Concurrency — REUSE, do not copy

The reference's `parallel()` (`workflow.ts:1313`) is fail-fast: one rejection kills the fan-out.
We want all-settled, because `agent()` returns `null` instead of throwing and one dead agent
should not kill 19 live ones.

| Need | Reuse | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Limiting, non-fail-fast | `mapWithConcurrencyLimitAllSettled` | `packages/coding-agent/src/task/parallel.ts:98` |
| Queueing, abortable | `Semaphore` (`acquire`/`release`/`resize`) | `task/parallel.ts:140` |
| Normalisation | `normalizeConcurrencyLimit` (`max <= 0` = unbounded) | `task/parallel.ts:135` |

**This is the Central Utilities rule.** Two implementations of the same thing is a bug even when
both work. Do not copy the reference's limiter.

The reference implementation to study for the shape of a fan-out is
`packages/coding-agent/src/cleanse/agent.ts:127-224` — it builds its own `ToolSession` from
scratch and shows the whole cycle (`dispatchWorker` at `:147-200`, `followUp` at `:201-212`).

## 3.4 Recursion — the cheap guard that prevents a fork bomb

`agent.ts:771`:

    export const DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_SUBAGENT_TOOLS = ["workflow", "workflow_control"];

A subagent that sees the `workflow` tool will spawn workflows, whose agents will see `workflow`,
forever. Use `subagentExcludedTools()` (`agent.ts:788`) and pass `blockedAgent` to the bridge.

## 3.5 Model routing — copy the principle, use OUR catalog

`src/model-routing.ts:73` (73 LOC): `meta.phases[].model` with `meta.model` as the default, via
`resolveModelForPhase`.

**AGENTS.md forbids hard-coding model-conditional policy in TypeScript.** The reference file obeys
this — it reads a string out of `meta` and consults a catalog. There is no `id.includes("claude")`
anywhere in it. Keep that property and route through `resolveModelPolicy` /
`buildModel` from `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog`.

## Tests

    test/workflow/agent-null.test.ts
      - a failing agent returns null and the SCRIPT CONTINUES      <- the contract
      - a failing agent does not throw out of agent()
      - agent() with a schema returns the parsed object, not a string
      - agent() with a schema whose result is empty-but-valid does NOT return null
      - an agent returning empty TEXT with no schema DOES return null (:2346)

    test/workflow/agent-structured.test.ts
      - status === "invalid" ⇒ surfaced as failure, NOT read as success   <- the #87501 shape
      - status === "unavailable" ⇒ surfaced as failure
      - the parsed-but-invalid payload is available for diagnostics

    test/workflow/recursion.test.ts
      - a spawned subagent's tool list excludes workflow + workflow_control
      - blockedAgent is passed through and enforced

    test/workflow/fanout.test.ts
      - one null among 20 does not cancel the other 19   <- all-settled, not fail-fast
      - the limiter is respected under load

title: P4 — Durability: JSONL delta journal, lease against two processes, resumable identity
description:
Journal-based durability. THIS PHASE LANDS BEFORE THE UI, deliberately — see "Why this order" below.

Copy source: `run-persistence.ts` (~300 of 790), `run-record-store.ts` (~250 of 500),
`workflow-paths.ts` (all 65), `fs-persistence.ts` (the `PersistenceFsLayer` interface only).

## Why we cannot reuse AsyncJobManager — measured, not assumed

`packages/coding-agent/src/async/job-manager.ts`, measured:

- **Four imports, ALL `import type`** (`:1-4`). Zero runtime imports — no `node:fs`, no
  `bun:sqlite`, no storage module.
- State lives in plain in-memory containers (`:254-264`): `#jobs = new Map`,
  `#deliveries`, `#evictionTimers`, ...
- `AsyncJobManager.instance()` / `setInstance()` (`:236-241`) is a **process-global singleton** —
  by construction gone on exit.
- Eviction is timer-based (`:954`), `DEFAULT_RETENTION_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000` (`:11`).

Resume is the feature's core. A substrate that dies with the process cannot carry it.

**`packages/durable` (`@ultraworkers/pi-durable`) exists and nobody uses it** — the async module
does not. MEASURE whether it fits before committing to it. Do not assume. If it does not fit, the
fallback is plain JSONL, which is what this bead describes.

## 4.1 On-disk format — copy `run-record-store.ts:99`

    FORMAT = "pi-workflow-run-v2"      ->  "ultraworkers-workflow-run-v1"
    <runPath>.events.jsonl             (:221)

Append-only, one JSON object per line. Each line is either:

- `HEAD` — a full snapshot, written when there is no prior line or on compaction
- `DELTA` — the difference from the previous line

`isHead` (`:103-105`) discriminates on `value.format === FORMAT`.

Bounds: `MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES = 8`, `MAX_CACHE_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024` (`:100-101`).

Supporting types: `Cells` (`:76`), `Delta` (`:77-83`), `Entry` (`:84-89`), `Cached` (`:90-98`).
Functions: `cellsOf` (`:136-159`), `deltaOf` (`:160-185`), `applyDelta` (`:186-217`).

Write with `{ flag: head ? "a" : "w", flush: true }` (`:370`) — the flush is what makes a crash
lose nothing.

## 4.2 Paths — copy `workflow-paths.ts` with ONE string changed

    // reference
    export const WORKFLOW_HOME_RELATIVE_DIR = ".pi/workflows";
    // ours
    export const WORKFLOW_HOME_RELATIVE_DIR = ".ultraworkers/workflows";

Resulting layout:

    workflowHomeDir()       -> ~/.ultraworkers/workflows
    workflowUserSavedDir()  -> ~/.ultraworkers/workflows/saved
    workflowProjectKey(cwd) -> `${slug}-${sha256(resolve(cwd)).slice(0,12)}`
    workflowProjectPaths()  -> ~/.ultraworkers/workflows/projects/<key>/{runs,saved}

`sanitizePathSegment` (`:64-65`): lowercase, `[^a-z0-9._-]+` -> `-`, strip leading/trailing `-`,
cut to 48 chars, fall back to `"project"`.

**Project-scoped state is isolated by a stable cwd-derived namespace** — the docblock at `:1-7`
explains why the home dir is used rather than scattering `.pi/workflows` into every project. Keep
that reasoning.

## 4.3 The lease — copy `run-persistence.ts:250-261`

    interface LockFile { runId: string; runPath: string; pid: number; startedAt: string; token: string }
    export interface RunLease { runId: string; token: string }

- `acquireRunLease(runId)` -> `RunLease | null` (null = someone else holds it)
- `token` = `crypto.randomUUID()`
- `recoverStaleRuns()` (`workflow-manager.ts:609`) scans for leases whose `pid` is no longer alive

Two ultraworkers processes in the same project must not both own one run. This is the guard.

## 4.4 Identity — copy `workflow.ts:892-914`, keeping the reasoning

    const callIndex = state.callSeq++;
    const deltaKey  = `${runId}:${callIndex}`;

`callSeq` **must stay lexical** — `:919` says it outright: *"gates deliberately: callIndex/agentCount
must stay lexical"*. Adding a conditional increment inside a branch makes resume replay the wrong
calls.

**`deltaKey` MUST include `runId`.** The comment at `:902-913` explains a real collision: a nested
`workflow()` restarts its own `callSeq` at 0, so a parent's `callIndex` 0 and a child's
`callIndex` 0 would collide. `deltaKey` is at once the `SharedStore` delta key **and** the event id
for `onAgentStart`/`onAgentEnd`/`onAgentHistory`. An unawaited stray `agent()` from the first child
can still be pending when the second child mints the same id.

Resume semantics (`:506`, `:624`):

- replay from `callIndex 0`
- `callIndex < firstMiss` -> cached result
- from `firstMiss` onward -> run live

## 4.5 Persisted state shape — copy the types

`run-persistence.ts:29` — `RunStatus = "pending" | "running" | "paused" | "completed" | "failed" | "aborted"`

`:31-58` — `PersistedAgentState`, with
`status: "queued" | "running" | "done" | "error" | "skipped"`.

`:61-69` — `PersistedJournalEntry`: `{ index, hash, result }`.

`:81-208` — `PersistedRunState`. Note it carries `sessionId`, `parentSessionId`, `parentSessionFile`,
`error`, `errorCode`, `pauseReason`, `resetHint`, `checkpoint`. **These session-identity fields are
Ours-to-decide** — the reference uses them for its navigator's "current session only" filter. If
our navigator shows all runs, they are dead weight; measure before carrying them.

`:284-297` — `PERSISTED_AGENT_STATUSES` plus an `AssertNever` exhaustiveness type. Keep the
exhaustiveness check; it is what makes adding a status a compile error rather than a silent hole.

`:310-324` — `terminalRunInterruptCause` and `settleNonTerminalPersistedAgents`: a run killed
mid-flight must settle its in-flight agents to a terminal status on next load, or the UI shows
`running` forever.

`:282` — `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES`, `:280` — `DEFAULT_MAX_TERMINAL_RUNS_ON_DISK = 300`.

## 4.6 Injectable fs — copy the INTERFACE only

`fs-persistence.ts` (210 LOC) defines `PersistenceFsLayer`, re-exported as `FsLayer`
(`run-persistence.ts:268`). The docblock says it is *"Exposed for testing - pass overrides to
inject mock implementations."*

Copy the interface. Do not copy the 210 LOC of node:fs implementation — the repo's Central
Utilities rule says use `Bun.file()` / `Bun.write()` and namespace `node:fs/promises`.

## Why this phase lands BEFORE the UI

The navigator shows `p` pause, `x` stop, `r` restart. Those are UI over things that must REALLY
exist. Build the UI first and `r` is a keypress that silently does nothing — which is worse than
the key not existing, because it teaches the user a lie.

## Tests

    test/workflow/paths.test.ts
      - project key is stable for the same cwd
      - two different cwds produce different keys
      - sanitizePathSegment handles spaces, dots, unicode, and a 60-char name

    test/workflow/store-format.test.ts
      - write HEAD, read back: identical state
      - write HEAD + 3 DELTAs, read back: identical to the direct snapshot
      - a truncated last line is tolerated (crash mid-append)   <- the real crash shape
      - FORMAT mismatch is detected, not silently parsed

    test/workflow/lease.test.ts
      - acquire succeeds when free; a second acquire returns null
      - release frees it
      - a lock file whose pid is dead is reclaimable

    test/workflow/resume.test.ts
      - run 5 agents, kill the process after 2, reopen, get the same final result
      - resume replays cached calls 0..firstMiss-1 without re-invoking them  <- the contract
      - from firstMiss onward, calls run live
      - a nested workflow's callIndex 0 does not collide with the parent's

title: P5 — Manager + workflow_control: state machine, object schema, structured errors
description:
The run manager and the `workflow_control` tool. Between them they own the state machine and the
error contract.

Copy source: `workflow-manager.ts` (~600 of 2412), `workflow-control-tool.ts` (~200 of 285),
`workflow-tool.ts` (~300 of 548).

## 5.1 WorkflowManager — copy the shape, cut the plumbing

`export class WorkflowManager extends EventEmitter` (`workflow-manager.ts:426`).

| Keep | ref line |
|---|---|
| `startInBackground` | `:682` |
| `runSync` | `:798` |
| `pause` | `:1726` |
| `attachCheckpointResponse` | `:1747` |
| `resume` / `stop` | ~`:1850` / `:1900` |
| `listLiveRuns` | `:554` |
| `recoverStaleRuns` | `:609` |
| `getSnapshot` / `getRun` | ~`:1350` / `:1400` |

Eleven events drive the UI's redraw (`:1996-2017`).

### CUT

- `adoptLiveRunsToSession` (`:570`) — their session-id ownership model
- `setModelRegistry` / `listAvailableModelSpecs` — replace with `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog`

### PERSIST BEFORE OBSERVE — the ordering that matters

`startInBackground` (`:748-776`) persists the INITIAL state BEFORE executing, and on persist
failure it releases the lease and deletes the run.

If execution starts first, a crash in the first millisecond leaves a run on disk that no process
owns and no one resumes. The reverse — a persisted run that then fails to start — leaves a
recoverable record.

`persistRun(managed, required = false)` (`:1577`) is the write path; `schedulePersist` (`:1524`) is
the debounced one. `required = true` means "this write must land or the run is not real".

### pause() returns false, does not throw

`pause` (`:1726-1735`):

    if (managed?.status !== "running") return false;

It also persists the requested state immediately but RETAINS the lease until `executeRun` settles
and writes exact abort-teardown usage. Copy that subtlety: releasing the lease on pause would let
a second process claim a run whose agents are still draining.

## 5.2 State machine — copy `workflow-control-tool.ts:216-229`

    running             -> [status, pause, stop]
    paused              -> [status, resume, stop]
    failed | pending    -> [status, resume]
    completed | aborted -> [status]

## 5.3 workflow_control — the two traps

**Trap 1: the schema must be an OBJECT, never a union.**

The comment at `workflow-tool.ts:8-15` is explicit: a discriminated `Type.Union` of two objects
serialises to a top-level `anyOf` with no `type`, and strict providers (DeepSeek is named) reject
it with *"schema must be type object, got type: null"*.

So: one object, `action` is the full verb set as a string union, `runId` is optional AT THE SCHEMA
LEVEL. The per-action requirement is enforced at runtime in `normalizeInput` (`:152-182`):

    const allowedKeys = input.action === "list" ? new Set(["action"])
      : input.action === "resume" ? new Set(["action", "runId", "checkpointId"])
      : new Set(["action", "runId"]);
    const extraKey = Object.keys(input).find(k => !allowedKeys.has(k));
    if (extraKey) throw new Error(`workflow_control action "${input.action}" does not accept ${extraKey}`);

`checkpointId` passed to `status` THROWS. This is a schema-level union expressed as a runtime
check because the wire format cannot express it.

Also: `additionalProperties: false` here (unlike the `workflow` tool's schema).

**Trap 2: errors are RETURNED, never thrown at the model.**

`:209-214`:

    result(`action=${action} result=error runId=${runId} error=${message} allowed=${allowed.join(",") || "none"}`,
           { action, result: "error", runId, error: message, allowedActions: allowed })

A thrown tool error is an opaque failure to the model. A returned structured error carries
`allowedActions`, so the model can recover without another round trip.

This is the same shape as bug #87501 — a message reporting `success: true` for something that
never happened. Errors travel as data.

## 5.4 No `rm` at tool level

`/workflows rm` exists only as a slash command (`workflow-commands.ts:286-289`). Deletion is
destructive and stays a human action. When a run is `active in another live session`, the slash
command says so explicitly.

## 5.5 formatRun — the machine-readable line

`:277-281`:

    runId=... name="..." status=... phase="..." checkpoint=<json>
    total= done= running= queued= error= skipped= active="..." tokens=[~]N

The `~` prefix on tokens when totals include character-heuristic estimates (`:262`,
`tokenTotalEstimated`).

`summarizeRun` (`:231-264`) prefers live snapshot data and falls back to the persisted record,
taking `Math.max` across live/persisted/aggregate token figures — so a resumed run does not
display FEWER tokens than it actually spent.

## Tests

    test/workflow/control-schema.test.ts
      - checkpointId + status THROWS                        <- trap 1
      - runId missing for pause/resume/stop THROWS
      - the emitted JSON Schema is type:object, NOT anyOf    <- trap 1, asserted on the SCHEMA
      - action=badvalue fails with the allowed list
      - a failing control returns result="error" + allowedActions, does NOT throw  <- trap 2

    test/workflow/durable-order.test.ts
      - the initial state is on disk before the first agent runs
      - a persist failure leaves no run on disk and no lease held

    test/workflow/state-machine.test.ts
      - pause on a non-running run returns false, does not throw
      - the allowed-action table matches each status
      - pause retains the lease until executeRun settles

    test/workflow/tokens.test.ts
      - a resumed run reports >= the tokens it actually spent   <- Math.max across sources
      - estimated figures carry the ~ prefix

title: P6 — UI: /workflows navigator (3 tiers), progress panel, token formatting
description:
The `/workflows` navigator and the progress panel. This is the largest UI surface — ~1200 LOC from
`workflow-ui.ts` plus ~400 from `task-panel.ts`.

Copy source: `workflow-ui.ts` (~1200 of 2346), `task-panel.ts` (~400 of 1782),
`display.ts` (~180 of 469).

## 6.0 Mount path — WHY we touch no core

`ctx.ui.custom()` (`packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/types.ts:404`) is a
full-screen, keyboard-focused component that returns a typed result. It already exists.

This is the concrete reason the whole epic needs zero core diff. We do NOT need to add an overlay
base class, a navigator seam, or a panel slot — `custom()` and `setWidget()` are the seams.

⚠️ **`setFooter`/`setHeader` throw outside the interactive TUI.** `hasUI` is NOT a valid guard — it
is `true` in RPC and in ACP-with-`elicitation.form`, and both throw (`types.ts:310-330`). The
correct guard is `canMount("header"|"footer"|"custom")` (`:324`).

## 6.1 The view stack — copy `workflow-ui.ts:108`

    runs --enter--> phases --enter--> agents --enter--> detail
         <--esc---        <--esc----        <--esc----

`ViewKind = "runs" | "phases" | "agents" | "detail" | "savedDetail"` (`:108`).
`StackFrame` (`:496-505`); `back()` pops (`:801-826`).

`phases` and `agents` share ONE two-pane frame; only the cursor differs (`:1217-1218`).

## 6.2 Keys — copy `keyToAction` at `:1891-1950`

| Key | Action | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `up`/`k`, `down`/`j` | move -1/+1 | `:1893-1900` |
| `pageUp`, `ctrl+u`, `ctrl+b` | page -1 | `:1901-1904` |
| `pageDown`, `ctrl+d`, `ctrl+f` | page +1 | `:1905-1908` |
| `home`/`g`, `end`/`G` | jump start/end | `:1911-1917` |
| `t` | toggleTail (detail only) | `:1918-1919` |
| `enter` | drill / togglePager | `:1920-1924` |
| `right` | drill / openPager | `:1925-1928` |
| `esc`/`escape`/`left` | back | `:1929-1932` |
| `q` | close | `:1933-1934` |
| `p` | pause (double-tap) | `:1935-1936` |
| `x` | stop (double-tap) / delete saved | `:1937-1939` |
| `/` | filter (runs only) | `:1940-1941` |
| `r` | restart / rename saved | `:1942-1943` |
| `s` | save | `:1944-1946` |

**THERE IS NO `f` KEY.** Grepping `"f"` in `workflow-ui.ts` returns nothing. Filtering is `/`.
`ctrl+f` is page-down. A reviewer who "fixes" this by adding `f` is adding an inconsistency.

`activeRunId()` (`:827-832`) returns the frame's `runId` when drilled in — so `p`/`x`/`r`/`s` stay
bound to the run at every depth, not just on the runs list.

### Text modes swallow every key — `:2102-2148`

`filter` and `rename` short-circuit BEFORE any browse binding runs. The comment states why:
*"This prevents pasted text, Unicode, or control sequences from leaking through to destructive
browse bindings."*

This is a correctness requirement, not a nicety. Without it, pasting a string containing `x` into
the filter box stops the run.

### Double-tap confirmation — `:2150-2162`, `:937-958`

`p` and `x` require a second press. `confirm()` re-validates action + cursor + filter + full
context against the CURRENT item, so a prompt opened on row 3 cannot execute against row 5 after
the list scrolls.

Manager events deliberately do NOT cancel a pending confirmation (`:652-656`).

## 6.3 Two-pane layout — copy `:1163-1290`

    +-- Phases --------------+-- <phase> - N agents ---------------+
    | > 1 research      2/3   | * reviewer-a      sonnet  35k      |
    |   2 verify        0/4   | * reviewer-b      sonnet  12k      |
    +-----------------------+------------------------------------+

- `computeLeftWidth` (`:1032-1050`) clamps to `[14, min(40, 45% of width)]`
- `RW = width - LW + 1` (`:1229`) — shared divider column
- Right box title is `<phase> - N agents` (`:1279`), or `"no agents"` when empty (`:1260`)
- Narrower than `LW_MIN + RW_MIN - 1` -> `renderSinglePane` (`:1316-1365`)
- Both panes scroll independently (`:1307-1313`); a trailing `...` row marks more (`:1250-1252`)

### The render loop — OUR contract, not the reference's

There is no observable/reactivity system in our TUI. The contract is: **mutate a private field, call
`requestRender()`** (`packages/tui/src/tui.ts:769`).

`render(width)` MAY return the SAME array reference to skip repainting (`tui.ts:237-242`), and
`describe()` must return the same `NativeNode` while unchanged (`tui.ts:245-247`).
`AgentHubOverlayComponent` does exactly this — `#native` field at `agent-hub.ts:455`, invalidated
in the `requestRender` wrapper at `:473-476`. Copy that pattern.

## 6.4 The panel — copy `task-panel.ts:1761-1780`

    ctx.ui.setWidget("workflow-tasks", renderPanel(...), { placement: "belowEditor" });

Compact (`:1501-1529`):

    Workflows running (2):
      * my-workflow  3/7 agents . research
      = other-flow   0/4 agents
      /workflows - open navigator (11 finished kept in history)

Only `running` + `paused` runs are listed as active. Finished runs drop off the live panel but the
hint COUNTS them, so a completed run does not look like it vanished.

Detailed (`/workflows-progress detailed`, `:1652-1711`): adds tokens, cost, and `~820 tok/s` from a
10s rolling window (`RATE_WINDOW_MS` `:1534`). The rate window survives pause->resume because
samples are keyed by persisted `runId` (`:1536-1537`).

### THE PANEL TAKES NO INPUT

`task-panel.ts:1761-1762`, verbatim: *"Purely informational: it lists running runs and re-renders
on events. To open the navigator, the user runs /workflows (the panel takes no input)."*

No `Focusable`, no `handleInput`, no focus/expand key. **Do not add one.** A focusable panel
competes with the editor for keystrokes; the whole point is that you keep typing while it runs.

## 6.5 Formatting — copy `display.ts:142-160`

`fmtTokenSegment` returns `""` when nothing is known, so a surface NEVER prints a false `0 tok`.
Prefix `~` for heuristic estimates. `fmtCost` floors at `"<$0.0001"`.

`compactTokens` (`:991-1001`): `842`, `35k`, `35.7k`, `1.3M`. Cache reads shown apart:
`89K tok - 3.0M cached`.

## What we deliberately do NOT show

| Absent | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Elapsed time in the navigator | grep `duration\|elapsed\|startedAt\|Date.now` in `workflow-ui.ts` returns NOTHING |
| A replayed/skipped badge | `WorkflowAgentSnapshot` (`display.ts:10-35`) has no such field |
| Panel input | `task-panel.ts:1761-1762` |

## Tests

    test/workflow/keybindings.test.ts
      - up/down/j/k move; enter drills; esc pops all three tiers
      - pasting a string containing "x" into the filter box does NOT stop a run  <- the contract
      - p then p pauses; p then Esc cancels
      - a confirmation opened on row 3 does not execute against row 5 after scrolling
      - "f" is not bound to anything; ctrl+f is page-down

    test/workflow/layout.test.ts
      - two panes at width >= threshold
      - ONE pane below LW_MIN + RW_MIN - 1                        <- the degradation path
      - left width clamps to [14, min(40, 45%)]
      - render() returning the same array reference skips repaint

    test/workflow/panel.test.ts
      - the panel registers belowEditor
      - finished runs leave the panel but remain counted in the hint
      - the panel does NOT implement handleInput                    <- negative contract
      - setFooter/setHeader are guarded by canMount, not hasUI

    test/workflow/format.test.ts
      - unknown token totals render "" not "0 tok"
      - estimated figures carry ~

title: P7 — User scripts from disk, approval gate, /ultracode, authoring skill
description:
User scripts from disk, the approval gate, `/ultracode`, and the authoring skill.

## 7.1 Reading scripts from disk — copy `workflow-saved.ts` + `builtin-workflows.ts:145-155`

Lookup order: **SAVED FIRST, BUILT-IN SECOND.**

`builtin-commands.ts:373-376`:

    const SHADOW_WHOLE_STRING_PRIMARY: Record<string, string> = {
      "deep-research": "question",
      "adversarial-review": "task",
    };

A user script shadows a built-in of the same name. `resolveWorkflowInvocation`
(`builtin-workflows.ts:145-155`) checks saved workflows first, then built-ins.

Locations: `~/.ultraworkers/workflows/saved/*.js` and the project `saved/` dir (see P4's paths).

### The security boundary — state it, do not imply it

Reading arbitrary scripts is executing arbitrary code. The vm realm is **NOT a security sandbox** —
copy the reference's own admission verbatim (`workflow.ts:516-528`): *"vm is not a security
sandbox — an injected bridge function's `.constructor` is still the host Function... best-effort
against ACCIDENTAL nondeterminism from trusted (user / guided-LLM) scripts, not a security wall."*

The boundary that DOES hold: scripts live only in user- or project-owned directories.

- **Never** download a script from a remote registry
- **Never** run another agent's script
- The extension loads scripts from paths the USER configured

This must appear in the docs and in the docblock, not be left for a reader to infer.

## 7.2 The approval gate — OUR design, NOT a copy

### What the reference actually has: a gate, but NOT the one we are building

MEASURED. `grep -rn "ui\.confirm|ui\.select" src/` returns TWO files, not one:

    src/workflows-models-command.ts   ui.select / ui.confirm  — model-tier config, unrelated
    src/workflow-tool.ts:258-265     ui.confirm               — THE WORKFLOW GATE

⚠️ **An earlier draft of this bead claimed only `workflows-models-command.ts` matched. That was
wrong**, and the shape of the error is worth recording: I grepped, got a plausible-looking single
file, and generalised to "no approval gate exists" — without reading what the other file's use of
`ui.confirm` was FOR. The gate was there the whole time.

The real code, `workflow-tool.ts:255-265`:

    // checkpoint() reaches the human only on a UI-bearing foreground run; a
    // background run is detached, so checkpoint() falls back to its headless
    // default. Map a checkpoint to ctx.ui.confirm (a yes/no gate) when available.
    const uiCtx = ctx as
      | { hasUI?: boolean; ui?: { confirm?(title: string, message: string): Promise<boolean> } }
      | undefined;
    const uiConfirm = uiCtx?.hasUI ? uiCtx.ui?.confirm : undefined;
    const confirm = uiConfirm
      ? (promptText: string) => uiConfirm.call(uiCtx?.ui, "Workflow checkpoint", promptText)
      : undefined;

So the reference DOES have a human gate. What it lacks is the thing we are building:

| | Reference `checkpoint()` | Our consent gate |
|---|---|---|
| When | MID-RUN, only if the script author calls it | BEFORE the run starts, unconditionally |
| Granularity | per call site in the script | per workflow fingerprint |
| Persistence | yes — journaled, replayable, resumable (`WorkflowCheckpoint`) | yes — `consent.json` |
| Headless | falls back to `options.default ?? true` | asks every time |
| Answers "may I ask you something?" | | answers "do I trust this script?" |

`checkpoint()` is strictly BETTER than a yes/no dialog once a run is underway, because it is
journaled and a resumed run replays the same answer. **We adopt it as-is** — it is already in the
19 globals, and P1/P4/P5 carry its plumbing (`WorkflowCheckpoint`, `attachCheckpointResponse` at
`workflow-manager.ts:1747`, the `status: "waiting" | "resuming" | "consumed"` lifecycle).

⚠️ **Note the headless fallback: `options.default ?? true`.** A background run with no UI
**auto-answers yes** (`workflow-tool.ts:1766-1773`). Copying that default silently makes a
headless run approve its own prompts. For a CONSENT gate that is the wrong default — pick the
default deliberately, and make it fail visible.

What the reference genuinely lacks (measured, still true):

- No `permissionMode`, no `allowAlways`, no "don't ask again" anywhere in `src/`
- `WorkflowSettings` (`:13-74`) has NO consent field
- `startInBackground` (`workflow-tool.ts:271-285`) calls the manager directly — no pre-run prompt
- No "View raw script" affordance beyond the read-only `savedDetail` render (`:1577-1579`)

⚠️ **What was mis-described in planning.** A four-option approval prompt with "don't ask again"
was attributed to this repo. It came from the Claude Code docs. The reference has one
yes/no checkpoint gate mid-run, not a consent dialog. We build ours because `ui.confirm` exists at
`types.ts:337` and we have permission modes — and now because `checkpoint()` proves the pattern.

### Design

- Ask **once per fingerprint**, where fingerprint = `sha256(script + toolset + cwd)`
- Store in `~/.ultraworkers/workflows/consent.json`, scope `user|project`
- `setFooter` shows current status: *"This workflow is approved for this project - `x` to revoke"*
- Revocation deletes the entry; the next run asks again

**Without persistence we ask EVERY time.** That is more prompting, not less. A gate that cannot
remember is not a convenience.

## 7.3 /ultracode — copy `effort-command.ts:71-87`

**It is a slash command, NOT a free-text keyword.** Measured: there is no detection of the literal
string `ultracode` anywhere in the reference's `src/`.

`/ultracode` sets `state.level = "ultra"` on a shared mutable object; `/ultracode off` sets it
back. **It never touches settings** — the state is in-memory only and survives reload via runtime
handoff (`pi-extension.ts:146-152`, `:194-199`). Any argument other than `off` turns it ON
(pinned by `tests/effort-command.test.ts:75-76`).

Both `/effort` and `/ultracode` emit under `customType: "effort"` (`:55`) — the TUI cannot
distinguish them. **This is worth doing better**: give ultracode its own `customType`.

### Auto-arming is a SEPARATE system

`workflow-editor.ts:303-384`, gated by `hasTrigger` (`:37-39`). The regex (`:32-35`) uses
lookbehind/lookahead excluding `/`, `\`, `$`, and Unicode identifier characters — so `myworkflow`,
`workflow_name`, and `src/workflow-editor.ts` do NOT trigger (`:22-30`).

`isSubstantive` (`effort-command.ts:45-48`): `text.length >= 16 && !startsWith("/")`.

The armed turn REWRITES the submitted text (`action: "transform"`), it does not inject a separate
message. `armReasonClause` (`:74-78`) states the trigger honestly — *"you typed the workflow
trigger word, which counts as an explicit opt-in"* vs *"standing effort mode armed this turn (you
did not explicitly ask for a workflow)"*.

### suppressedKeywordText — an escape hatch with NO producer

Declared `workflow-editor.ts:50`, read once at `:338-339`. **Every write in `src/` assigns
`undefined`** (`:178`, `:190`, `:209`, `:220`). Only a test ever sets a value
(`tests/workflow-editor.test.ts:724`).

So there is NO dismissal UI in the shipped reference. If we keep the field we must add a real
producer; otherwise delete it rather than shipping a declared-and-never-set flag.

## 7.4 The authoring skill — copy SELECTIVELY

Keep:

    SKILL.md
    references/runtime.md
    references/helpers.md
    references/common-helpers.md
    references/quality-helpers.md
    references/retry-helper.md
    examples/fan-out-and-synthesize.js
    examples/structured-output.js
    examples/adversarial-verification.js
    examples/phased-budgets.js
    examples/validated-gate.js
    examples/loop-until-done.js

DROP:

    references/registry-ownership.md   (describes THEIR ownership model)
    references/versions.md
    references/review.md
    references/debugging.md            (references files that do not exist for us)

`runtime.md:7` is the normative authoring rule — quote it in our docs:

> *"Start with the only legal export: `export const meta = { name, description, phases?: [{ title,
> detail?, model? }] }`. Values are nonblank literals; declare only used phases and call `phase()`
> before each phase's work. The remaining body already runs inside an async function: write
> helpers as ordinary declarations; `export default` and other exports are invalid. Return the
> result explicitly."*

## 7.5 The six quality helpers — copy `workflow.ts:1468-1630`

| Helper | Signature | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `verify` | `(item, opts?: { reviewers?, threshold?, lens? })` | `:1468` |
| `judgePanel` | `(attempts, opts?: { judges?, rubric? })` | `:1507` |
| `loopUntilDry` | `({ round, key?, consecutiveEmpty?, maxRounds? })` | `:1545` |
| `completenessCheck` | `(taskArgs, results)` | `:1588` |
| `retry` | `(thunk, opts?: { attempts?, until? })` | `:1605` |
| `gate` | `(thunk, validator, opts?: { attempts? })` | `:1619` |

Each calls `ensureAgentCapacity()` BEFORE running — slot count is `reviewers`,
`attempts.length * judges`, or `1`. `maxAgents` must cover the whole run tree.

`verify` defaults to `threshold ?? 0.5` and its prompt says *"Default to real=false when
uncertain"* (`:1485`). `retry` returns the LAST result when attempts run out (`:1615`) — the caller
inspects it.

## Tests

    test/workflow/consent.test.ts
      - first run of a fingerprint ASKS
      - second run of the SAME fingerprint does NOT ask
      - a different script, toolset, or cwd ASKS again
      - revoking deletes the entry and the next run asks
      - consent.json survives a process restart

    test/workflow/registry.test.ts
      - a user script SHADOWS a built-in of the same name
      - scripts load from user and project dirs
      - a script outside those dirs is NOT loaded          <- the security negative contract

    test/workflow/ultracode.test.ts
      - /ultracode sets ultra; /ultracode off clears it
      - any other argument turns it ON
      - it does NOT write to settings
      - a reload preserves the state

    test/workflow/helpers.test.ts

      - judgePanel: attempts.length * judges slots reserved
      - loopUntilDry: stops after maxRounds and on consecutiveEmpty
      - retry: returns the LAST result when attempts exhaust
      - gate: feeds validator feedback back into the next attempt

    test/workflow/arming.test.ts

      - "workflow_name" does NOT trigger
      - "workflow" DOES trigger
      - a 10-char message does not count as substantive

title: P8 — PROOF: zero core diff, five seams reached, a third-party extension runs unmodified
description:
THE ONLY CONDITION THAT PROVES THIS EPIC CORRECT.

## Definition of done

    git diff <base>...HEAD -- packages/    # MUST be empty

Not "should be empty". Not "empty except for a doc comment". **Empty.**

## Why this is last but not optional

The other seven phases can ALL be green with the extension in the wrong place. A workflow engine
that lives in `packages/coding-agent/src/workflow/` passes every unit test in the world and still
fails AGENTS.md's criterion, because the criterion is about WHERE the code lives, not whether it
works.

This session produced that exact shape twice:

- `epic-jwsy.11` — a correct, tested, never-reached peer fence. `api.registerPeerFence` was
  never called because `registerPeerTools` had no production caller.
- `epic-jwsy.14` — a baseline gate that abstained (VOID) and exited 0, so a CI badge read "pass"
  while no verdict was reached.

Both were green. Both were inert. Neither was visible until a falsifier was written.

## What to assert

### 1. The literal diff

    git diff <base>...HEAD -- packages/

Byte-count must be zero. Changelogs under `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` are NOT exempt — if this
feature needs no core change, it needs no core changelog entry either.

### 2. The five seams, each REACHED (not merely present)

A symbol that exists but is never called reads as decomposed while being inert. Assert:

| Seam | Reached by |
|---|---|
| `registerTool` | registering `workflow` and `workflow_control` |
| `registerCommand` | `/workflows`, `/ultracode` |
| `registerSetting` | a workflow preference |
| `on(...)` | `input` (arming) + `session_start` (panel install) |
| `setWidget` | the progress panel, `placement: "belowEditor"` |

### 3. Behavioural proof — the layer that cannot be faked

Boot the host with the extension loaded and assert observable consequences:

- `/workflows` appears in slash-command completion
- `workflow` appears in the tool list
- a setting round-trips through the settings panel
- a lifecycle hook's EFFECT is observable (not that it was registered)

### 4. AGENTS.md's wording — a third-party extension must work too

The strongest form of the proof: a MINIMAL extension written against only the public
`ExtensionAPI` type, in its own directory, registering a tool + command + setting + hook + panel,
runs with no core change. If that is possible, the seam is real. If it needs a core edit, this epic
failed regardless of how many tests pass.

## AGENTS.md: never source-grep

This bead must NOT assert `expect(src).toContain("registerTool")`. That tests how code LOOKS, not
what it DOES — it passes on a comment and fails on a reflow.

`git diff` over paths is a statement about the commit, not a string match, so layer 1 is fine.
Layers 2 and 3 must assert BEHAVIOUR: a registry that lists the name, a completion list containing
it, a hook whose effect is observable.

Reading a file your own code WROTE (a generated manifest, a fixture) and asserting on that output
is explicitly fine.

## Also required before closing

    bun run check:ts
    bun run --smoke-test        # MUST be unchanged: we added no worker selector
    br dep cycles               # MUST be empty

The smoke test is the check that no worker was added. Workflows run IN-PROCESS via
`runStructuredSubagent`. If `--smoke-test` needs a new probe, something spawned a process that
should not have been spawned — which is the `pi-subagents` trap.
notes:
## SỬA LẠI CHÍNH MÌNH TÔI: §18.7 #4 và #5 ĐÃ CÓ, tôi đã báo "không tìm ra" vì grep sai thư mục

Tôi báo anh là "#3 và #5 tôi không đo". **#5 sai, và nguyên nhân là grep của tôi có phạm vi hẹp**:

```
grep -rn "atomicWriteJson|deriveEndpoint|envelope" packages/peer/src/transport/   → 0
```

`atomicWriteJson` **không** nằm trong `transport/`. Nó ở `inbox/store.ts:148`. Và §18.7 #4 + #5
đã có test thật, trong `inbox-crash.test.ts`:

- **#5** "the documented loss is asserted, not skipped" → `inbox-crash.test.ts:16-20` (docblock tự
  nêu), `:117` (prefix liên tục sau SIGKILL thật), `:128` (gap BÁO CÁO được, không phải im lặng).
- **#4** `atomicWriteJson` + EPERM → `:173` (retry), `:201` (hết budget ⇒ reject, file cũ còn nguyên).

Đây là `a-zero-is-about-the-set-you-searched` lần thứ ba trong phiên này. Zero là về **tập tôi tìm**,
không phải về codebase.

## §18.7 #3 — thật sự CHƯA có, và tôi đã viết test (20629b15a)

Đo đúng: **không hàng test nào bảo vệ**. Cả 9 hàng cũ trong `transport-send.test.ts` đều bind **một**
endpoint và giao cho **một** target (`"BlueLake"`). Nên một transport đọc address từ envelope sẽ
vẫn xanh cả 9.

Tính chất **đã đúng sẵn** — đọc code là biết: `createPeerSocketTransport` tính `endpoint` một lần từ
`deps` (`send.ts:202`), và `sendFrame(endpoint, frame)` nhận address làm tham số **tách khỏi** frame.
Không hàm nào nhận cả hai rồi đọc cái này ra từ cái kia. **Đó chính là lý do nó cần test**: "đúng sẵn
theo cấu trúc" là phát biểu về `deliver` hôm nay, và bản vá dễ dàng (2 dòng, typecheck không ý kiến,
không hàng test nào phản đối) là route theo `target`.

Ba hàng, mỗi hàng một chủ đề:

| hàng | nội dung |
|---|---|
| `delivers to the derived socket even when the target is another project s address` | address độc lậch; target là **đường dẫn socket của project khác** |
| `stamps its own id…` | `deliver(target, message)` không nhận sender ⇒ không field nào giả mạo được người gửi |
| `puts no address on the wire…` | khung dây đúng tập key ⇒ không có gì để receiver tương lai tôn trọng |

### Bài học đo được, ghi lại vì tôi đã làm sai một lần

Mutation đầu tiên tôi chọn là `${endpoint}.${target}` (address per-target). Nó **giết cả 3 hàng** —
vì hướng đó làm HỎNG chính việc giao, không phải chỉ giao sai chỗ. Hàng chết vì "không có listener",
mà mọi hàng giao tin đều chết vì lý do đó ⇒ **số hàng chết là thuộc tính của mutation, không phải bằng
chứng về hàng**. Đã viết lại R1 để **address sai vẫn sống và vẫn ack**, rồi đo lại:

```
M2 from<-target                          → chết ĐÚNG hàng attribution
M3 thêm endpoint vào body                 → chết ĐÚNG hàng shape
M4 transport dựng cho project kia (test-side) → chết ĐÚNG hàng address
M1 sendFrame(target, frame)              → chết cả 3 (collateral: R2/R3 target không có listener)
```

Và dưới M1, hàng address chết **đúng chỗ cần chết** — không phải vì giao hỏng:

```
298 | expect(outcome).toEqual({ outcome: "persisted" });        ← XANH (peer giả mạo đã ack)
303 | expect(homeMessage).toMatchObject({…})                    ← ĐỎ, received null
```

Tức redirect xảy ra và hàng bắt được nó. Đo tay, không suy.

### Một đằng khác đáng ghi: POSIX không dùng `projectDir` cho address

```
peerEndpoint(projectDir, runtimeDir)  →  win32: pipe có hash projectPath
                                       →  posix: path.join(runtimeDir, "peer.sock")   ← projectDir BỎ QUA
```

Nên câu chữ "target tên session ở project khác" trong plan là framing **Windows**. Trên POSIX hai
project khác nhau chỉ khác `runtimeDir`. Cả hai test đều đúng, nhưng **tên hàng không được bán
oversell**: nó nói "project" trong khi đo là "runtime dir".

`packages/peer`: **269 pass / 4 skip / 0 fail** (trước 266). `check:types` sạch.

## §18.7 #6 — ĐÃ HỎNG THẬT, đã sửa (`f0e279c32`). Wrong join thứ hai trong plan

Đo trên store như nó đang đứng, không đọc từ plan:

```
acquireLease(C:\Repo\src, exclusive)  → GRANTED
acquireLease(c:\repo\SRC, exclusive)  → GRANTED      ← MỘT file NTFS, HAI owner
```

`path_pattern` so với COLLATE BINARY mặc định của SQLite ⇒ chữ hoa/thường không hề đi vào so sánh.

**Plan tưởng là đã xử lý** (`docs/peer-messaging.md:3991`: "NTFS is case-insensitive | Already handled —
§3.2 puts uniqueness in the store"). Đó là **wrong join**, cùng hình lần fence: §3.2 nói về **NAME
store**, còn `path_pattern` là chuỗi khác trong bảng khác. Hai phát biểu đều đúng, câu nối thì sai.

### Sửa: chuẩn hoá một lần ở **write**, không phải `COLLATE NOCASE`

`COLLATE NOCASE` ở 4 chỗ ngắn hơn và **sai trên POSIX**: `/repo/A` và `/repo/a` là hai file, nên fold sẽ
**từ chối** một lease mà caller hợp lệ xin. Chuẩn hoá lúc ghi làm `acquireLease`, `findConflicts`,
`listLeases`, `listLeaseHistory` nhất trí **theo cấu trúc**.

Schema **v3 → v4**. Không bump thì store v3 thoát sớm khỏi `migrate()` và không bao giờ được backfill ⇒
defect chỉ tái xuất hiện trên DB đã nâng cấp. Backfill viết lại **qua JS**, không dùng `lower()` của
SQL: SQLite chỉ fold ASCII, nên hai nhánh của **cùng một phép so sánh** sẽ bất đồng với path
không-ASCII.

### Hai hàng cũ ghim `user_version === 3` và **đúng là đỏ**

Chúng là tripwire có chủ đích. Đổi sang **literal 4**, KHÔNG đổi sang `SCHEMA_VERSION`: so với hằng thì
một lần bump mà không thêm gì cũng xanh, đúng thứ hai hàng đó sinh ra để làm lộ.
**Đã kiểm tra tripwire còn răng**: bỏ `PRAGMA user_version = ${SCHEMA_VERSION}` ⇒ cả hai đỏ.

### Phạm vi coverage — nói thẳng

| cái | verify ở đâu |
|---|---|
| **luật** fold/exact của `leasePathKey` | **mọi platform** (mode là tham số, không đọc `process.platform` ẩn) |
| **hợp đồng POSIX** (2 hoa/thường khác nhau = 2 lease) | end-to-end, mọi platform — hướng một fix sai sẽ hỏng |
| **hệ quả DB của `fold`** (acquire thứ hai bị TỪ CHỐI) | **KHÔNG assert** — chỉ quan sát được nơi default là `fold`, tức Windows |

Không có hàng `skipIf(win32)` cho hệ quả đó: nó sẽ đọc như có coverage và không chạy ở đâu — đúng hình
hai hàng pipe Windows tôi vừa chuyển đi ở `98ababcd2`.

## Bài học mới: mutation giết **0** hàng cũng là dữ liệu

Tôi viết một hàng "không phụ thuộc locale" (vì `toLocaleLowerCase` biến `I` thành `ı` ở locale Thổ
Nhĩ Kỳ). Nó **xanh**. Mutation `toLowerCase → toLocaleLowerCase` **giết 0 hàng**.

Đo mới biết vì sao: `LANG=tr_TR.UTF-8 LC_ALL=tr_TR.UTF-8 bun -e '"I".toLocaleLowerCase()'` → `"i"`,
`Intl` default vẫn `en-US`. Locale resolve lúc **khởi động process**, không đọc `process.env` giữa
test; child process cũng không giúp. ⇒ Đã **xoá** hàng đó. Hàng không thể chết tệ hơn không có hàng:
nó chứng nhận **không cái gì**.

**Câu tổng quát:** mutation giết 0 hàng thường nghĩa là **công cụ không chạm tới tính chất** trên máy
này, không phải tính chất an toàn. Đối xứng với "số hàng chết là thuộc tính của mutation, không phải
bằng chứng về hàng": cái trước nói về **độ rộng**, cái sau nói về **độ sâu**.

`packages/peer`: **275 pass / 4 skip / 0 fail**. `check:types` sạch.

title: [TRAP] Two recorded traps: the forbidden worker-spawn architecture, and deep-research that does not verify
description:
A recording, not a task. Both entries are DECISIONS already made — this bead exists so a future
agent does not reverse them by reading only the reference repo.

## TRAP 1 — `pi-subagents` has the architecture our rules forbid

`.tmp/ref/pi-subagents` solves the same problem with the opposite architecture.

| | `pi-dynamic-workflows` | `pi-subagents` |
|---|---|---|
| Execution | in-process in a `node:vm` realm | `workflow/worker-source.ts` (781 LOC) GENERATES SOURCE then spawns processes |
| Orchestration | `workflow-manager.ts` (2412) | `agent-manager.ts` (1581) |
| Widget | `task-panel.ts` (1782) | `ui/agent-widget.ts` (659) |

AGENTS.md forbids exactly that shape:

> **Worker scripts**: workers re-enter the CLI entrypoint; never spawn separate worker entry
> modules.

That rule was written after issue #1150, where `with { type: "file" }` copied the entry as a raw
asset and workers **crashed silently in compiled binaries** (issues #1011, #1027). The later
literal-path + extra-entrypoint pattern required keeping spawn literals and two build scripts in
sync — which is issue #1150's own fix.

**Copying the `pi-subagents` branch copies the defect the rule exists to prevent.**

## Our decision: in-process, no new worker

Workflows run via `runStructuredSubagent` inside the host process. Consequences:

- **No new worker selector.** All 16 existing selectors derive from
  `WORKER_HOST_SELECTOR_PREFIX` (`packages/utils/src/worker-host.ts:18`), split between
  `cli/worker-selectors.ts` (8) and `cli.ts` (8, declared locally to keep their module graphs lazy).
- **`cli.ts` is untouched.** No dispatch-table entry, no argv selector.
- **`--smoke-test` is unchanged.** The 14 existing probes stay at 14. If a new probe is needed,
  something spawned a process.
- **`ci:test:smoke` and `scripts/install-tests/run-ci.sh` are untouched.**

If a future bead needs a worker, it must first argue why in-process execution is impossible. The
answer is usually "it is not".

## TRAP 2 — `deep-research` does not verify, despite the name

`src/deep-research.ts:61-67`, the ENTIRE Verify phase:

    phase('Verify')
    const verdict = await agent(
      'Cross-check these research sources. Group claims that assert the same fact across different
       source URLs. Keep a claim only if it is supported by at least ' + minSupport + ' distinct
       source URLs OR by one clearly authoritative source. ...',
      { label: 'cross-check', schema: { supported: [...], discarded: [...] } }
    )

Measured facts:

1. **One agent, one pass.** No voting, no independent verifiers, no re-fetching.
2. **`minSupport` (default 2, `:34`) is INTERPOLATED INTO THE PROMPT**, not enforced in code. The
   model is asked to honour it.
3. **The `OR by one clearly authoritative source` clause means a claim can pass on ONE source.**
4. **`verdict.discarded` is DROPPED.** The schema requests it (`:66`); the return statement never
   reads it (`:77`).

There is NO `unverified` bucket, NO `refuted` bucket, NO per-claim status field. The string
`refuted` appears nowhere as a data field.

## Adversarial voting DOES exist — in a different file

`src/adversarial-review.ts:45-62`:

    parallel(findings.map((f, i) => () =>
      parallel(Array.from({ length: reviewers }, (_, r) => () =>
        agent('You are a skeptical reviewer. Try to REFUTE this finding... Default to real=false
              when uncertain. ...', { label: 'refute ' + (i+1) + '.' + (r+1),
                                      schema: { real: boolean, reason } })
      )).then((votes) => {
        const valid = votes.filter(Boolean)
        const realCount = valid.filter(v => v && v.real).length
        const ratio = valid.length ? realCount / valid.length : 0
        return { finding: f, realVotes: realCount, totalVotes: valid.length,
                 survives: ratio >= threshold }
      })
    ))

`refuters * findings` agents total. Survives iff `ratio >= threshold` (default `0.5`, `:36`).

The runtime's `verify()` (`workflow.ts:1468-1500`) is the same shape generically, with an optional
`lens` rotation.

## Decision

**`deep-research.ts` is CUT** (see the cut-ledger bead). **Copy `verify()` + `judgePanel()`**
instead — `:1468-1630`, part of the P7 helper bead.

If someone later wants a real deep-research workflow, it is `verify()` plus fan-out, not a copy of
`:61-67`.

title: P0 — Extension entrypoint: register tool, commands, settings, hooks, panel (the seam itself)
description:
THE SEAM ITSELF. This is the bead that makes "zero core diff" possible rather than merely claimed.

Copy source: `src/pi-extension.ts` (~120 of 378 LOC — the registration portion only).

## Why this is its own bead and not a detail of another

Every other bead builds a file. This one is the file that PLUGS ALL OF THEM INTO THE HOST.

It is also the single bead whose failure mode is invisible: if it is wrong, every sibling unit test
still passes, because each sibling is tested in isolation. The engine works. The contract works.
The navigator renders. And the user gets none of it, because nothing was ever registered.

That is `epic-jwsy.11` again: `registerPeerTools` had no production caller, so
`api.registerPeerFence` was never called, so the fence was never installed — and every test was
green.

## What to register

    // extensions/workflow.ts
    export default function activate(pi: ExtensionAPI, ctx: ExtensionContext) {
        // 1. TOOLS
        pi.registerTool(workflowTool);            // the workflow builtin
        pi.registerTool(workflowControlTool);     // lifecycle control

        // 2. COMMANDS
        pi.registerCommand("workflows", { ... }); // the navigator + verbs
        pi.registerCommand("ultracode", { ... }); // standing maximal-effort mode

        // 3. SETTINGS
        pi.registerSetting({ id: "...", ... });   // workflow preferences

        // 4. HOOKS
        pi.on("input", armingHandler);            // keyword arming
        pi.on("session_start", installHandler);   // panel + manager wiring

        // 5. UI SURFACES
        // ctx.ui.setWidget("workflow-tasks", ..., { placement: "belowEditor" })
        // ctx.ui.custom(...) for the navigator
    }

Copy the shape at `pi-extension.ts:161-378`: `installResultDelivery` (`:161`), both
`registerTool` calls (`:178-179`), `on("session_shutdown", ...)` (`:183`),
`registerEffortCommand` (`:253`), `on("session_start", ...)` (`:257`), `installTaskPanel` (`:355`),
`installWorkflowKeywordArming` (`:361`), `on("model_select", ...)` (`:374`).

## The `session_start` subtlety

`:257-279` does NOT install the panel immediately — it waits for `session_start` and re-installs
there (`:279`). The reason is lifecycle: an extension's UI surfaces registered before the session
exists can be dropped by a session switch.

`:294-297` applies `"defaultEffort": "ultra"` from settings ONCE, guarded by `effortInitialized`
so a settings default does not clobber an in-session `/effort` choice.

Copy both guards. The second one is a user-visible behaviour (a session default must not stomp a
choice made this session) and is exactly the kind of thing that gets dropped as "redundant".

## `on("model_select")` — `:374`

The workflow manager caches the main model for agents that inherit it. A model switch mid-run must
update it (`:661` `setMainModel`) or every subsequent agent routes to the old model.

## `session_shutdown` — `:183`

Runs are persisted on disk. On shutdown the manager must settle in-flight agents to a terminal
status (`settleManagedInterruptedAgents`, `:1539`) so the next session does not show `running`
forever.

## Registration order

`registerEffortCommand` at `:253` comes BEFORE the `session_start` hook that installs arming
(`:361`). The arming hook reads `effort.level`, so the state object must exist first.

A registration-order inversion here produces a hook that reads `undefined` — and it will not throw,
it will just silently never arm.

## The manifest

    package.json:
      "pi": { "extensions": ["extensions/workflow.ts"],
              "skills": ["skills/workflow-authoring"] }

## Tests — this bead's tests are REACHABILITY, not unit tests

    test/extensions/workflow-seam.test.ts
      - the extension activates without error
      - AFTER activation, "workflow" is in the tool list          <- reached, not merely defined
      - AFTER activation, "workflow_control" is in the tool list
      - AFTER activation, "/workflows" is in slash-command completion
      - AFTER activation, "/ultracode" is in slash-command completion
      - the workflow setting appears in the settings panel and round-trips
      - firing session_start installs the panel widget

Every row asserts the CONSEQUENCE of registration, not that a registration call appears in a file.
AGENTS.md bans source-grep tests: `expect(src).toContain("registerTool")` passes on a comment and
fails on a reflow.

## What a failure here looks like

Not a red test — a **green** epic that ships nothing. If this bead's reachability assertions pass
individually but nothing calls `activate()`, the tests pass. Wire an assertion that the extension
MANIFEST is loaded and `activate` ran.
